title: Paged Holistic Query Reservoir with Tenant Priority Smoothing
creator: Daniel Kim
description:
Problem: Console dashboard query APIs are suffering high tail latency and read amplification for mixed tenant workloads. Large scans (long paginated explorations) dominate I/O and create unfairness where low-SLA tenants cause hotspots that increase latency for higher-priority customers. Current paging implementation opens many small DB cursors and issues repeated scans for backfills, causing amplified reads and high CPU on analytic nodes.

Goal: Implement a "query reservoir" layer that coordinates pagination across workers, reduces duplicate scan work with a small bounded prefetch reservoir, and applies tenant-priority smoothing so committed/high-SLA tenants receive stable latency while still allowing exploratory traffic. Success metrics: 30% reduction in read amplification for paginated endpoints, 95th percentile latency improvement of at least 20ms across heavy workloads, and measured fairness (weighted 95p latency) improved for high-priority tenants.

Approach:
- Add a lightweight reservoir coordinator in the query service that tracks active paginated cursors and deduplicates overlapping page ranges. The coordinator exposes a token-bucket per-tenant that enforces soft concurrency limits and priority weights.
- Implement a small per-worker cold-path microcache for first-page and common prefix results (TTL ~15s) to cut cold start costs without long-lived staleness.
- Use dynamic page-size adaptation: increase page size when downstream consumer latency budget allows, decrease when overloaded.
- Hedge reads for long-tail pages by allowing a bounded speculative fetch (up to +1 page) when latency isolation is poor, with automatic cancellation when another worker serves the page.
- Add index-hinting and lightweight partition-aware prefetch for tenants with known hot segments (via recent access heatmaps), reducing scan ranges.
- Telemetry: instrument per-tenant tokens, reservoir hit/miss, read amplification ratio, memory footprint, and hedged-fetch cancellations. Expose these in Grafana and set alerts on increased read amplification or memory pressure.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end 95p latency for paginated dashboard queries improved by >=20ms on representative multi-tenant load.
- Read amplification (measured as logical rows scanned / rows returned) reduced by >=30% on staging cluster.
- Resource overhead for reservoir + microcache <10% memory increase on query nodes.
- Canary rollout plan and feature flag present; automatic fallback to current behavior if errors or memory pressure exceed thresholds.

Rollout plan: spike -> implement in feature branch -> internal benchmark on staging with controlled tenants -> canary (5% of traffic across 2 clusters) -> measure metrics for 72h -> 25% -> 100%.

Risks and trade-offs: additional complexity in coordinator and potential single-point throttling; trade between per-worker caches (simpler, lower cross-worker coordination) and shared cache (Redis) with higher consistency and memory visibility. We will start with per-worker microcache + coordinator to minimize operational changes.
